newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rostelekom cuts phone tariffs to U.S..
newsitem.headline: Rostelekom cuts phone tariffs to U.S..

text.p: Russian telecoms company Rostelekom said in a statement it would lower the cost of telephone calls to the United States by 57 percent from November 1 to January 15.
AOOT Mezhdugorodnoi i Mezhdunarodnoi Elektricheskoi Svyazi Rostelekom said it had been able to lower tariffs because of measures taken to increase access to the network.
Rostelekom has a market share of some 85 percent for outgoing international calls, analysts say. In this sector, the greatest demand is for transatlantic calls, Rostelekom said.

Between 8 p.m. and 8 a.m., the tariff for one minute would be cut to 4,200 roubles from 9,800. Day-time calls would cost 6,300 instead of 14,700 a minute and calls at weekends and holidays would cost 3,150 roubles instead of 7,350 a minute.

"A flexible tariff policy is a new strategy, allowing Rostelekom to satisfy the demands of all clients and to compete on the market for international services," the statement quoted chief executive Oleg Belov as saying.
The PRP Group, responsible for Rostelekom's public relations, said the volume of outgoing international calls from Russia was expected to rise in 1996 to 340 million minutes from 290 million in 1995.
PRP said the tariff cut, which covers the busy Christmas period when demand is high, was a first step, and it did not exclude that the reduction might be extended.
Rostelekom shares were at $2.46 on the Russian Trading System at 1320 GMT, compared to Monday's close at $2.43.
